subject: Question on error when truncating a distribution - Code provided

messages.author: 3e911bc3bc76c82d
messages.subject: Question on error when truncating a distribution - Code provided
parts:
Hi all!

I am doing some tests about a specific structure to be part of a bigger model and I am having some problems with them. The code to reproduce the error is at the end of the message.

My aim is to estimate the parameters of a distribution from a vector that is composed of observed and unobserved (NA) values, that is, vec = c(10, NA, 11.3, NA, 1, NA...).

I am interested in providing different truncation points for different values of the vector:

for (i in 1:nvec){
vec[i] ~ T(dgamma(shape = sh, rate = ra), 0, truncvalue)
}
sh ~ dgamma(1,1)
ra ~ dgamma(1,1)

Truncvalue being a vector with a truncation value for each value of vec (100, 20, 35, 30...).

I wonder if with this approach it is possible to infer the parameters of a distribution. I am also interested in imputing values to the NAs. I am having a recurrent error when building the model and I cannot understand which the problem is - I cannot see why the model would interpret "ra" is of dimension 0.

 Error in genVarInfo3() :
  Dimension of ra is 0, which does not match its usage in 'Dist[i] ~ dgamma(shape = sh, scale = lifted_d1_over_ra, .rate = ra, lower_ = 0, upper_ = truncvalue[i], .mean = lifted_d1_over_ra * sh, .sd = lifted_d1_over_ra * sqrt(sh))'.

The code to reproduce the error is below. Thank you very much and any advice will be very appreciated. 

Best, 
Jaume.

#CODE#####
sc <- nimbleCode({
 
  for(i in 1:nind){
    vec[i] ~ T(dgamma(shape = sh, rate = ra), 0, truncvalue[i])
  }
 
  sh ~ dgamma(1,1)
  ra ~ dgamma(1,1)
})

#Simulated data: vector of values
vec <- rgamma(500, 1, 0.1)
for(i in 1:length(vec))
  vec[i] <- sample(c(vec[i], NA), 1, TRUE, c(0.6, 0.4))

#Simulated data: truncation values
truncvalue <- numeric(length = length(vec))
truncvalue[!is.na(vec)] <- vec[!is.na(vec)] + 2
truncvalue[is.na(vec)] <- runif(length(truncvalue[is.na(vec)]), 0.1, 55)

#Data
my.data = list(vec = vec, truncvalue = truncvalue) #known-states matrix
#Constants
my.constants = list(nind = length(vec))

#Creating initial values for "vec" vector
initsvec <- vec
lengthin <- length(initsvec[is.na(initsvec)])
initsvec[is.na(initsvec)] <- rgamma(lengthin, 1, 0.1)
initsvec[!is.na(vec)] <- NA

#Initial values
my.inits <- function(){list(
  vec = initsvec,
  sh = rgamma(1,1),
  ra = rgamma(1,1)
)}

#Parameters to save
parameters <- c("vec", "sh", "ra")

 my.model <- nimbleModel(sc, data = my.data, constants = my.constants, inits = my.inits())

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Question on error when truncating a distribution - Code provided
parts:
Hi Jaume,

This seems to be caused somehow by providing 'truncvalue' in 'data' rather than in 'constants'. I'm going to file an issue for us to look into, as it will take a bit of time for us to see what is going wrong.

It should work for you if you put 'truncvalue' into the 'constants' rather than 'data'.

-chris
